descs.t: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate race, and former Congressman Hansen Clarke followed her. Michigan voters on camera say her move changed their vote. We walk through what she said and how her party answered.

Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, now says he is unfit to serve in the Senate and is campaigning for Mike Rogers. CNN reports that multiple House Democrats are privately pushing to expel her from their caucus. We look at what her break means for the Michigan race.

Haley Stevens said she does not like seeing the Democratic nominee campaign with somebody who said America deserved 9/11, and she backed Mike Rogers. Her party turned on her, and some Michigan Democrats are following her anyway. This is the fight inside the Democratic Party on Election Day.

intro.plain: Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for Senate in Michigan, over her own party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Then former Congressman Hansen Clarke did the same. Voters on camera say it gave them permission to switch. It is Election Day, so this matters right now. Chat, tell me: is crossing party lines an act of conscience, or a betrayal?
intro.mid: Haley Stevens lost the Michigan Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed by about one percent. Now she calls him unfit for the Senate and is campaigning for Mike Rogers. CNN reports some House Democrats want her out of their caucus. On Election Day, the question is whether Democrats follow her. Chat, if you are in Michigan, did her move change anything for you?
intro.bold: A sitting Democrat looked at her party's Senate nominee, saw him standing with somebody who said America deserved 9/11, and said no. Haley Stevens backed Mike Rogers, and her own party went after her for it. Some Michigan voters say she gave them permission to switch. Chat, would you have had the guts to do what she did?

hook.plain: A Democratic congresswoman just endorsed the Republican in Michigan's Senate race. Here is what Haley Stevens said, who followed her, and how her party answered.
hook.mid: Haley Stevens lost the primary by about one percent. Now she is campaigning for the other side. Here is why, and what it could mean for Michigan's Senate race.
hook.bold: She was called a traitor for saying no to Abdul El-Sayed. Haley Stevens did not back down, and some Michigan Democrats are following her. Here is the whole fight.

descs.t: The US Supreme Court has rejected the Trump administration's emergency request to make California set aside roughly 20,000 mail ballots from voters the federal government flagged as likely noncitizens. A federal judge, James Boasberg, had already blocked the Justice Department's demand. We walk through what was asked, what the courts decided and what it means for Tuesday's count.

The Supreme Court turned down the Trump administration's bid to have California sideline about 20,000 mail ballots the Justice Department says may have come from noncitizens. Critics of the request say the federal data is flawed, while the administration says noncitizen voting dilutes lawful votes. We look at both claims and what the ruling settles before the midterms.

The Trump administration wanted roughly 20,000 California mail ballots set aside as likely noncitizen votes, and the Supreme Court said no. A US attorney says 34 noncitizens in California have now been charged with illegally registering and voting, while Gavin Newsom calls the federal push intimidation. We break down the fight over who gets counted on the eve of the vote.

intro.plain: Big ruling right before Tuesday. The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's emergency request to make California set aside about 20,000 mail ballots the federal government flagged as likely noncitizen votes. A federal judge had already blocked the same demand. So those ballots get counted. Chat, do you think the court got this right?
intro.mid: The Supreme Court just said no to the Trump administration on California's ballots. Washington wanted roughly 20,000 mail ballots from suspected noncitizens set aside; the court refused, after Judge Boasberg also blocked the Justice Department. Critics say the federal list is flawed, the administration says noncitizen votes dilute lawful ones. Chat, which side has the stronger case?
intro.bold: Twenty thousand flagged ballots, and the Supreme Court says California counts them all. The Trump administration called them likely noncitizen votes, a US attorney says 34 noncitizens in the state have already been charged, and Gavin Newsom calls the push intimidation. This is a fight over who gets to decide an election. Chat, where do you stand?

hook.plain: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to set aside roughly 20,000 California mail ballots. The court refused. Here is what was asked, why it failed and what happens to those ballots.
hook.mid: Two courts, one answer: California keeps counting about 20,000 ballots the federal government flagged as likely noncitizen votes. Here is the case each side made and what the ruling settles.
hook.bold: Thirty four noncitizens charged, 20,000 ballots flagged, and the Supreme Court still says count them. Here is the ballot fight in California the night before the country votes.

descs.t: A federal judge in Alaska has dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit over the state's Senate race, where a second Dan Sullivan appears on the ballot beside Republican Senator Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola. The DOJ says it will appeal. We walk through what the suit asked for, why it was thrown out, and what happens next.

Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the DOJ's Decoy Dan lawsuit in Alaska, and the department says it is appealing. President Trump says Chuck Schumer and Marc Elias should be held responsible for the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, while one poll shows Peltola and Sullivan tied at 50 percent. We look at how a duplicate name could matter under ranked choice.

Two men named Dan Sullivan are on Alaska's Senate ballot, a court just tossed the DOJ's attempt to step in, and Trump calls it election fraud at the highest level. With the race tied in one poll, every confused ballot could count. We break down the fight, the appeal, and whether voters can trust the result.

intro.plain: A federal judge in Alaska has thrown out the Justice Department's lawsuit over the Senate race, where a second Dan Sullivan is on the ballot next to the real Senator Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola. The DOJ says it will appeal. So what was the suit about, and does it change anything before the vote? Chat, have you ever seen two candidates with the same name on one ballot?
intro.mid: Alaska's Senate race has two Dan Sullivans on the ballot, and a judge just dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit over it. Chat, tell me: is this a dirty trick or a nothing story?
